_NUMBERING: Turkey's corpus build ended at batch 15. This work runs 16-25. Batch 16 (S-insure) is written and gated.
_DOCTRINE: Report mechanics, never make the call. check-noconnect.py exit 0 before import. A null fact DELETES its sentence. Dates are drift-prone: every one goes in a fact-span, and NONE goes in a title, heading or excerpt — those cannot carry a span.
_THE_BET: S-calendar is the speculative swamp: 0 dedicated words and only 6 passing mentions in 72 articles. One of those mentions — getting-around-turkey's 'allow buffer time around the two major Bayram holidays' — is a WARNING with a single right answer, not a decision. Gate A after this batch decides whether a real decision sits underneath the warning, or whether the book runs on six swamps instead of seven.
_WHAT_WOULD_MAKE_IT_A_DECISION: A warning becomes a decision when the reader faces a genuine trade-off with more than one defensible answer. The candidate here: the observance itself barely affects a visitor, while the two Bayram travel surges affect them enormously — and the surges move about 11 days earlier each year, so which season they collide with changes annually. That is a collision with S-regional-season, and the articles must report both halves WITHOUT joining them.

articles.title: Ramadan in Turkey: What Actually Changes for Visitors
reports: when Ramadan falls and that it moves earlier each year against the solar calendar
what stays open: sites, museums, transport, tourist-area restaurants
what changes: some daytime dining, alcohol service in some venues, working hours
how observance differs between Istanbul, the coastal resorts and the conservative interior
the etiquette a visitor is actually expected to observe, and where
articles.must_not_say: whether to avoid travelling during Ramadan — that is the reader's call and, if it connects to season, the book's

articles.title: The Two Bayram Holidays and How Turkey Travels
reports: the two Bayrams, what each marks, official duration in days, and how the gap between them works
that both move earlier each year against the solar calendar
the domestic travel surge: who travels, in which direction, and what fills
which parts of the country empty and which fill
government and bank closure versus what stays commercially open
articles.must_not_say: any margin or buffer rule, any 'avoid these dates', any sequencing advice

articles.title: What Closes on a Turkish Public Holiday
reports: the full national public-holiday calendar with fixed dates
the legal closures: banks, government offices, post
museums and archaeological sites — which close, which run holiday hours
the Grand Bazaar and covered bazaars, which follow their own rule
transport on a public holiday versus a Bayram

articles.title: How Turkey's Holiday Calendar Is Actually Set
reports: the three separate authorities: Diyanet declares the religious dates, Law 2429 fixes the public-holiday duration, and a presidential decree adds anything extra that year
why religious dates stay provisional until close to the time, and what moon sighting has to do with it
the arife half-day rule and the 3-full-days / 4-full-days structure written into law
that extra administrative leave and toll-free periods are decided year by year, not by standing rule
the toll-free mechanism when it is granted: KGM-operated bridges and motorways, free municipal transport, and BOT crossings excluded
articles.must_not_say: how far ahead to book, how much slack to leave, or that a given year will have toll-free days
articles.note: This is the article most likely to drift into the call. The existing corpus already says 'allow buffer time'; this article must report the SELL-OUT MECHANICS and stop there.
articles._REPLACED: Was 'Booking Domestic Travel Around the Bayram Surge'. ALL SIX transport facts came back null from both panels — demand surge, booking lead time, bus/rail behaviour, ferry behaviour and fare behaviour are simply not published. The article could not be written without inventing them. This replacement is built only on what is sourceable: the legal and procedural machinery behind the calendar.

articles.title: Iftar and Ramadan Dining in Turkey
reports: what iftar is, when it happens, and how restaurants handle it
the pide bread queues and the seasonal dishes that appear only then
sahur and what is open before dawn
booking behaviour at iftar time in restaurants that serve it
how tourist-area dining differs from neighbourhood dining during the month
articles.must_not_say: that Ramadan is a good or bad time to eat in Turkey

pass_conditions: at least 3 articles carry a genuine option structure rather than a single-right-answer warning
cross-swamp joins (excluding S-calendar itself) between 1 and 4
gate_A.on_failure: Drop S-calendar. Redistribute batches 18-25 across the six known-open swamps and accept ~34-36 pages rather than pad. This is a planned outcome, not a setback.
gate_A.verdict_pending: Run after the five are written. The transport half of the S-calendar thesis is unevidenced and has been dropped from the corpus; what remains is the calendar-collision half.
